title: UK's New Social Media Ban: What Happens to Roblox and YouTube?
summary: Imagine waking up one day and finding out you can't use your favorite apps anymore. That's what's happening to kids in the UK! The government just announced a new rule: anyone under 16 won't be allowed on big social media platforms like Snapchat, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, X, and YouTube. But here's the twist—what about Roblox? Roblox is super popular with kids, but the government hasn't said yet if it's included. They're still figuring out the details. The UK is copying Australia's ban, which also blocks Kick, Reddit, Threads, and Twitch for under-16s. But Australia left out gaming sites like Roblox. So maybe the UK will too? One internet law expert, Lorna Woods, says it's not clear yet. Even if Roblox isn't banned, it will have to turn off features that let strangers talk to kids. That's a new rule for all gaming services. And YouTube? It's banned, but YouTube Kids is safe. Still, no one knows how they'll stop kids from just searching YouTube without an account. YouTube says it's a great learning tool and worries kids might go to less safe sites if banned. The government promises to keep educational stuff available, but we'll have to wait until July for more answers.
why_it_matters: This could change how you talk to friends online, so it's important to know if your favorite apps might be blocked.

background_read: Many countries have set age limits to protect kids online. Australia already bans under-16s from platforms like Snapchat, TikTok, and Instagram.
The UK has a law called the Online Safety Act, which tries to make the internet safer. Roblox is a game platform where players create and share their own games and chat with others.
Lorna Woods, an expert in internet laws, helps explain tricky rules about technology and what kids can access.
Article_Structure: WHO: UK government, kids under 16, social media companies
WHAT: A new ban stops under-16s from using big social media platforms, with Roblox undecided
WHY: To copy Australia's ban and protect kids, but details are still being figured out

perspectives.description: The UK government wants to keep children safe from harmful content, so they are blocking apps that might expose kids to danger.
Many kids enjoy using these platforms for fun, learning, and talking with friends. A ban could make them feel left out or unable to connect.
YouTube believes it is a helpful learning tool and worries that if kids can't use it, they might visit less safe websites instead.
